doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: How he knew the traditional tunes
summary: He knew old standards from his grandmother's radio, which let him anticipate melodies and changes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: How did you learn the music?

That’s an interesting question. That’s an excellent question. Because I don’t know. But I didn’t make any effort to learn the music but what happened was I used to sit by my grandmother at night and she would play the radio. And on the radio all these tunes would come on like “Bye Bye Blackbird,” and “Do You Know What it Means to Miss New Orleans?” And some kind of way I knew all these tunes so when I went to Your Father’s Moustache those were the tunes they were playing. And I kept feeling well why do I know these tunes? I don’t know. But I knew the tunes some kind of way, so I was kind of like adapt and play the changes to the songs because I knew how the melody was about to go. That’s a great question.
You knew how the melody was about to go—

I knew the melodies of these songs so I mean I had some idea to know kind of which way the chords were about to change to. You know? Inevitably most those songs go to a five chord or a four chord first of all.
And the tricky part was when it went to the relative minor then it went through the changes to get back to the major key again. But for the most part I knew a lot of these songs.
